sources.supports: C. monoculus mainly along the Solimões-Amazonas and the lower courses of its tributaries; its Rio Negro specimens are from near Manaus (as reported in the review)

designNotes: Placed in flooded forest (fish of lakes and tributaries, codes B and D, enter it at high water); the checklist records it in habitats BD. Occurrence pass: peak moved from dawn to the middle of the day: feeding is heightened 9 am to 3 pm (IGFA). Occurrence pass: lower while the water rises (0.7), because peacocks are lethargic in rising water (IGFA). Review: the genus revision puts this species mainly in whitewater floodplains, with its Rio Negro specimens near Manaus; the middle Negro sport-fishing study lists it. Kept, at low confidence. Kept sellable by design (Andy, 25 November 2026), although sport fishing in Amazonas is catch-and-release by law; the field guide says so.
